Alex / NetOps — tagging in some technical clarifications ahead of the deep-dive to make the meeting productive.

Short answers up front:
- For a customer that must centralize egress logging into their SIEM, Privatelink typically gives better observability and simpler network controls because traffic stays inside the cloud provider secure fabric and can be routed through a dedicated proxy/ALB that you control. Peering is possible but requires additional egress NAT and log forwarding work. For Solstice's SIEM-forwarding requirement, Privatelink is my recommendation.

- Ports & allowlist (initial):
  * Control plane (management): 443 (HTTPS) outbound to Redwood control endpoints. Allowlist prefixes (control plane): 13.59.78.0/24, 52.204.120.0/24 (we will confirm final list in runbook).
  * Data plane (model inference): TCP 443 to customer-configured endpoint when using Privatelink + internal ALB. For peering, you'll expose private subnets and allow specific source CIDRs from Redwood worker pools (we'll provide ranges).

- Allowlist rotation: Redwood commits to a minimum 30-day notice before changes to control-plane egress prefixes. For data-plane we offer two options:
  1) Stable static prefixes for Dedicated/Private with predictable ranges (recommended).
  2) Short-lived dynamic ranges + an allowlist umbrella if you prefer autoscaling without change windows.
  We'll document both approaches in the runbook and mark which approach maps to which hosting mode.

- TLS/KMS: We support TLS end-to-end. If you require on-prem KMS/HSM, we can integrate via customer-managed KMS using cross-account IAM roles and provide an exchange checklist for keys and rotation policies. Note: HSM on-prem will require slightly longer onboarding (3-4 weeks) for secure key provisioning.

Prep for the meeting:
- Please upload your annotated network diagram to the Drive link Hannah provided.
- Share the principal/name/email of the NetOps engineer who will be on the call.

I will bring a short runbook outlining: Privatelink wiring, recommended ALB/SNI configuration, port list, egress/routing examples, and post-change verification steps.

— Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
